role: SessionRecoveryCoordinator extension for recovering sessions from the app's own on-disk/iCloud backups, the trash, the H10's internal recording (workout/overnight augment, interrupted-workout auto-recovery) and paused-state restore; plus file-scope helpers and the InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery in-flight registry. The one-time merge-data-loss repair lives in RRCollector+MergeRepair.swift.
types: SessionRecoveryCoordinator.WatchRouteRecoveryResult: enum — recovered/distanceOnly/noRoute/failed outcome of Apple Health route recovery
SessionRecoveryCoordinator.StrapAugmentResult: enum — merged/notConnected/noStrapData/failed for workout strap merge
InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery: enum — lock-protected static set of session ids currently being auto-recovered at launch
AutoRecoveryAttempts: enum (file-private, @MainActor) — the launch auto-recovery attempt counter, one UserDefaults dictionary holding only the workout being recovered
state: ud:reviewedRecoveredWorkoutIds (static let reviewedRecoveredKey, string array capped at 50)

ud:autoRecoverAttempts (AutoRecoveryAttempts.key: [uuidString: Int] holding only the workout being auto-recovered; replaced on each counted attempt, removed on its successful recovery). Per-session 'autoRecoverAttempts_<uuid>' keys written by earlier versions are no longer read or removed
toplevel: Declares the three result enums inside the extension; file-scope private helpers unrecoveredBackupIds/newestWorkoutBackup; the file-private AutoRecoveryAttempts enum (UserDefaults key 'autoRecoverAttempts', limit 3); InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery enum with a static lock initialised to an empty set.

branches.effect: current session id inserted; otherwise skipped
paused session id inserted; otherwise skipped

branches.effect: recorder session id inserted; otherwise skipped

Restores a trashed session: un-marks it deleted (and tells iCloud trashRestore); if the archive still holds the id as deleted (the un-mark failed, which the service only logs) it logs the cause, abandons the iCloud restore and returns nil without rebuilding (the archive would refuse the write). Otherwise puts back the trashed file if the trash kept it, else rebuilds from the raw backup; on rebuild failure abandons the iCloud restore.

branches.cond: id still in archive.deletedIds after the un-mark

branches.effect: restoreFromTrashFailed abandons the iCloud restore (the un-mark is not rolled back); returns nil

units.does: Puts a trashed session's kept file back: loads it from the trash, links/supersedes any same-night session recorded since, archives it with skipSameNightMerge, discards the trash copy, marks its raw backup archived, force-reuploads to iCloud and bumps the archive signal.

branches.effect: continues; nil → returns nil (caller falls back to raw-backup rebuild)
logs error and returns nil (trash copy kept); caller then tries raw-backup rebuild

Deletes everything the session exported to Apple Health over its recording span (HealthWriteAndObserve.removeExports); true when every removal worked, false (logged at error level) when any failed.
writes: hk:the session's exported samples and workouts (deleted)

units.does: Pass-through to SessionRecoveryService.deleteLostSessions: marks each id deleted in the archive and returns the ids whose mark was stored.

Returns the session only when the rebuild was archived (outcome.wasArchived): then it bumps the archive signal and sets the review/trim card on MorningCoordination. Nothing rebuilt, or an archive write that failed, returns nil with no card and no signal.

branches.effect: returns nil with no review card and no archive signal; otherwise publishes and returns outcome.session

branches.effect: continues; otherwise returns nil (disk backup only)

units.does: Review/trim card Save: reads the archived workout, clips its RR series at endSec and re-finalizes it through WorkoutRecoveryService (discarding backups). Returns true when the card closed, false when it stays up with nothing saved (discardable). An archive read that throws logs an error and returns false, leaving the card up and the session unreviewed. With <30 beats left (including a session no longer in the archive) it keeps the workout untrimmed, closes the review (marked reviewed) and returns true. When the re-finalize returns nil or is not archived it logs an error and returns false, leaving the card up and the session unreviewed so the trim can be saved again; once archived it bumps the archive signal, closes the review and returns true.

branches.effect: returns false; card stays, session not marked reviewed

branches.cond: clipped.count < 30 (session not in the archive or without beats included)
branches.effect: closes the review (marked reviewed) and returns true

branches.cond: WorkoutRecoveryService.recover returned nil or outcome.wasArchived is false
branches.effect: logs; returns false; card stays, session not marked reviewed
notifies archive signal, closes the review, returns true

units.does: Reads the archived session and returns its RR points with t_ms <= endSec*1000: [] when the session is not in the archive or has no rrSeries; nil, after logging an error, when the archive read throws.
Marks the recovered workout reviewed (so its card does not come back) and clears the review card.

Review card Discard: deletes the archived recovered workout (failure logged via attempt). Only when the delete landed does it bump the archive signal, close the review and return true; a failed delete returns false and leaves the card up and the session unreviewed so Discard can be retried (discardable result). The raw backup is kept either way.

Recovers a crash-shortened workout's route/distance from Apple Health: with a Watch workout GPS route (>=2 points) it re-finalizes with that track (.recovered once archived, .failed when not); with no route, HealthKit passive walking/running distance if it beats the recorded distance by >50 m (.noRoute when it does not, .failed when the rewrite is not archived).

branches.effect: rebuilds with that track; otherwise falls to passive distance

branches.cond: recoverWorkout with the track returned nil (nothing rebuilt or not archived)
branches.effect: returns .failed, no fallback to the distance path

branches.cond: recoverWorkout with that distance returned nil (nothing rebuilt or not archived)

branches.cond: recover returned nil or outcome.wasArchived is false

branches.cond: WorkoutRecoveryService.recover returned nil or outcome.wasArchived is false

branches.effect: beat count falls back to merged.count

units.does: 'Pull from strap & re-merge' for an overnight scored from the stream: unless already device/composite-sourced, reconnects, downloads the strap's recording of this night, merges via DataSourceSelector (device preferred), persists the merged series + provenance, then re-scores through the saved-session reanalysis the caller hands in.

branches.effect: returns .noStrapData (also when refused because the strap's recording is considered live, see pullStrapRecording)

branches.effect: uses the persisted-but-unrescored session for source and beats; score reported nil

units.does: Begins a strap transfer (BLE hold) and reconnects for it; returns whether the reconnect succeeded.

Downloads the strap recording that belongs to an archived session (started during it), placed on the session's clock; refuses while a live session owns the strap; a downloaded recording dated outside the session (or undated) is handed to the rescue backup (rescueToBackup) instead, and the log says whether that backup landed. A failed one leaves the strap's copy unsaved, so the next start rescues it rather than clearing it.

Launch auto-recovery of a crashed workout. Before any await it claims the workout the persisted marker names (claimFlaggedWorkout), so the launch alert's Save waits on it; when the alert's Save or Resume claimed it first, returns and leaves the recovery to it. Then finds the interrupted workout (marker or newest backup) and registers that too. If the attempt budget (3) remains and the strap is reached, still records and no other recording has started, it counts the attempt, rebuilds via recoverWorkoutFromBackup and on success clears the marker and the attempt count. Both registrations end when it returns.

branches.cond: the flagged workout is already claimed (the launch alert is recovering it)

branches.effect: returns (registration of the flagged id ends)

branches.cond: attempt budget exhausted, or strap not reached / not recording / a new recording started
branches.effect: returns without counting an attempt; marker left for the manual card
returns leaving marker and count; otherwise clears both

units.does: True with no flagged workout. Otherwise claims it (InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery.claim) and returns true; when it is claimed already (the launch alert's Save or Resume), logs and returns false.

Whether launch auto-recovery may pull the strap: the strap is reconnected and still records (strapReadyForAutoRecovery), and the persisted marker does not now name a different session (a workout started while the strap was being reached). Logs and returns false otherwise.
